appraisal_events.evidence: « Elle n'a pas dû être mal, Mme Verdurin, et puis c'est une femme avec qui on peut causer, pour moi tout est là. Évidemment elle commence à avoir un peu de bouteille. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville values Mme Verdurin as good conversational company, which is what matters most to him, but frames the compliment with a patronizing aside about her fading looks/age.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Mais Mme de Crécy, voilà une petite femme qui a l'air intelligente, ah ! saperlipopette, on voit tout de suite qu'elle a l'oeil américain, celle-là ! [...] Je me figure que comme corps de femme... »
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville openly admires Odette's apparent intelligence and allure, though the praise is delivered in crude, objectifying terms and trails off into an appraisal of her body.

status_effects.explanation: Forcheville's remark positions her as valued company despite a backhanded note on her age, yielding a mild net-positive local appraisal.
She is singled out and admired by Forcheville for intelligence and allure, a mildly favorable local reception, though the terms are objectifying.

ambiguities: The narrator's simile likening M. Verdurin's and Mme Verdurin's laughter to 'deux masques de théâtre' could suggest an ironic diminishment of the sincerity of their hospitality, but this description is folded into the reception of Cottard's joke already captured in the accepted annotation, so it was left unscored to avoid duplicating that movement.
